title: Resource donation interface
description: No direct sharing mechanics (no shared stockpiles or shared victory). Instead a simple interface to donate resources to another player. Players handle negotiations themselves.

title: Per-player stance: shoot on sight / leave alone
description: Interface to designate each other player as shoot on sight or leave alone, like alliances in Red Alert but with no shared victory condition. Hostility is already decided in one place, Game.is_hostile.

title: Rule-based AI diplomacy
description: Without multiplayer, cohabitive play rests on the AI players. They need rules for donating, setting stances, and reacting to other players' donations, stances and attacks.

title: Emoji / gesture communication, no text chat
description: Players communicate only through emoji or gestures. No text chat: it causes more problems than it is worth. The AI players should send and react to these signals too.

title: Networking and multiplayer state
description: Networked multiplayer. New territory for the user, so interesting to explore. The simulation already runs in fixed ticks and every action goes through Game command methods, a starting point for lockstep (send commands, not state).

title: Pushback priority: workers push friendly units away from resources
description: Add priority to pushback. Workers push friendly units that are standing next to resources out of the way, so idle or parked units do not block mining spots.

title: Harvesting generates hazards: ents from wood, fire pits from crystal
description: Collecting resources wakes up the environment. Cutting enough wood turns trees into ents that attack whoever is closest (not necessarily whoever cut). Mining crystal makes fiery pits appear that spawn the red creeps. Not all resources need to be dangerous. Interplayer dynamic: overharvesting pushes danger onto neighbours, which gives players something to negotiate about. Not easy to add yet. Open questions: (1) resource types: at least wood and crystal; separate currencies or one stockpile? (2) disturbance tracked locally per area or globally per resource type? (3) ent wake-up rule: which trees, after how much cutting; does an ent remove its tree? (4) where fire pits appear, whether they can be destroyed; do timed waves stay as background pressure or get replaced? (5) is there a safe but slow resource?
